newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan inflation to fall to 120 pct - minister.
newsitem.headline: Sudan inflation to fall to 120 pct - minister.

text.p: Sudanese Finance Minister Abdel Wahab Osman was on Tuesday quoted as saying that inflation would drop to 120 percent by the end of the year.
Some economists say Sudan's liberalisation policy is fuelling inflation -- last estimated at 163 percent for the year to the end of July.
But Osman, quoted by the government newspaper al-Ingaz al-Watani, said the government had stopped deficit financing and started strict monetary measures to curb inflationary pressures.
He added that subsidising fuel was costing his ministry 10 billion Sudanese pounds ($6.9 million) every month.
Inflation is the main problem for Sudan and the government has made fighting it a top priority.
The war in the south against Christian and animist separatists is exhausting the country's financial resources.
The Islamist-dominated military government has managed to alienate most of its neighbours and international partners.
The United Nations has slapped limited sanctions on Sudan for failing to extradite three men charged with trying to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in 1995.
Contacts have been made with international financing institutions, including the International Monetary Fund, but none of them has given funds to Sudan, Osman said.

He did not expect ties with international and regional finance institutions to be normalised because he said they were demanding Sudan reconsider its Islamist orientation. "This is impossible," he added.
